rules.message: The posterior corneal surface must be more curved (smaller radius) than the anterior surface.
The pupil must leave at least 1.5 mm of iris on each side.
The iris root should be hidden under the limbus: iris diameter at least the visible corneal diameter.
A dilated pupil cannot be smaller than the undilated pupil.
The lens equator must fit within the corneal diameter.
Lens thickness must be less than its posterior radius or the lens shape is impossible.
Central anterior chamber depth below 1 mm is a flat chamber, which the renderer does not model.
Shallow central chamber: angle-closure risk. Expected in angle-closure cases.
The globe plus the conjunctival fornix fillet must reach 0.2 mm beyond the edge of the lid opening, or rays inside the opening miss every surface.
Central corneal thickness under 400 um is unusual outside ectasia or refractive surgery.
The lower tear meniscus should not be taller than the lid margin it rests on; a higher meniscus means epiphora or obstruction.
The optic disc must lie nasal to the macula, not on it.
The foveola must be smaller than the fovea.
The fovea must be smaller than the macula.
Retinal arteries are normally narrower than the veins.
The cup must stay inside the disc.
